newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan crime rate jumps 80 pct in six years.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan crime rate jumps 80 pct in six years.

text.p: Taiwan's social order has deteriorated to a "shocking" level, with the crime rate jumping 80 percent in six years, Interior Minister Lin Feng-cheng said on Monday.
The number of crime victims has jumped 60 percent since 1990, Lin told a government-sponsored anti-crime conference.
"The society is paying heavy prices for the shocking deterioration of social order," Lin said in his report.
In November, gunmen burst into a Taiwan county magistrate's home and shot dead the official and seven others in one of the island's most sensational crimes in recent memory.
In another brutal murder, women's rights activist Peng Wan-ju died after being stabbed more than 30 times in the southern county of Kaohsiung in November.
Both cases have remained unsolved and the government has been bitterly criticised by the public and the media for failing to maintain social order.
"We hope (the anti-crime conference) can demonstrate the government's determination to crack down on crime," Vice President Lien Chan, who doubles as premier, said at the conference.

The justice ministry in August launched an island-wide crackdown on crime gangs that Justice Minister Liao Cheng-hao said had infiltrated Taiwan's business and political circles and even parliament, triggering fears of underworld reprisals.
A police report has said the island of 21 million people has 10,582 gangsters belonging to 1,236 crime gangs.
As of mid-December, the justice ministry said it has questioned 316 gang members and detained 136 of them, including 53 government officials.
